No missing source prevents any consumer's own method, and no critical identity boundary is unresolved: the reporting entity is the consolidated registrant, named the same way on the cover of every filing (the 10-K prints file number 1-3579 and the 10-Qs 1-03579, the same registrant). The limitations below are source gaps, not findings about downstream analysis, which has not been done. Each limitation is carried into every consumer.

facts.label: Source-by-source assessment
facts.text: - 10-K FY2025. Entity: Pitney Bowes Inc., Delaware, "Commission file number: 1-3579" (page:1). Audited consolidated statements for 2025, 2024 and 2023 (pages 64-67), an opinion that internal control over financial reporting was effective ("maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025", page:62), debt Note 13 (pages 97-101), segment note (pages 83-84) and the exhibit index (pages 56-60). Part III is incorporated by reference from a proxy statement not supplied ("Portions of the registrant's proxy statement to be filed within 120 days", page:2). It records out-of-period corrections ("During the fourth quarter of 2025, we identified an error and recorded an out of period adjustment of $5 million", page:69) and the deconsolidated Global Ecommerce business (page:85). - 10-Q Q1 2026. Same entity; three months ended 2026-03-31. Debt table at page:18, covenant text at page:19, cash interest at page:24, segments from page:27. States that segment results were revised for a cross-border contract effective April 1, 2025 (page:5). - 10-Q Q2 2026. Same entity; three and six months ended 2026-06-30. Debt table at page:19 (includes a revolver balance of $96.7 million at 2026-06-30), debt narrative and covenants at pages 20 and 36. - 10-Q Q3 2026. Same entity; three and nine months ended 2026-09-30; "135,554,541 shares of common stock" outstanding at October 20, 2026 (page:1). Statements pages 2-4, debt Note 10 pages 19-22, pensions Note 11 pages 22-23, contingencies Note 13 page:24, liquidity page:34, covenants pages 20 and 36, exhibits page:39. - Releases. Each release is a management summary of one quarter with segment tables and a non-GAAP reconciliation (Q3 release pages 8-9: adjusted EBIT, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow). The Q3 release carries guidance and a debt-reduction statement. They are attributed management claims; adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow are management definitions.

facts.label: Source-risk mechanisms and downstream consequences
facts.text: - Covenant headroom. Evidence: three maintenance tests are printed, including a total net leverage maximum of "no greater than (a) 4.75 to 1.00 for each of the fiscal quarters in 2026" and compliance ("At September 30, 2026, we were in compliance with these financial covenants.") (Q3 10-Q page:20). Mechanism: each ratio is "as defined in the credit facility agreement", and no reported ratio, EBITDA definition or net debt definition is printed. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 cannot compute headroom and must write Not calculable; any ratio they build from adjusted EBITDA is not the covenant ratio. - Maturity labels and dates. Evidence: the Q2 10-Q says the term loan maturity was extended "to March 2031" (page:20) and the revolver was extended to March 2031 (page:20); the Q3 10-Q describes the same Q2 event as an extension "to May 2031" and the revolver "matures in May 2031" (page:20). Mechanism: the sources do not say that a later amendment changed the date; the Q3 10-Q exhibit list shows a Fifth Amendment dated September 29, 2026 (page:39) and the Q2 10-Q lists a Third and a Fourth Amendment (page:40), none of which is supplied. Consequence: the maturity wall must show the Q3 reading as latest filed, flag the Q2 difference, and not state the reason. - Revolver capacity. Evidence: a $450 million facility and "remaining borrowing capacity of $427 million" (Q3 10-Q page:20). Mechanism: the $23 million difference is not itemized; the 10-K says letters of credit reduce borrowing capacity ("Outstanding letters of credit reduce the amount we can borrow under our revolving credit facility", page:45) and gave about $27 million at 2025-12-31, but no 2026 letters-of-credit amount is printed. Consequence: liquidity must use $427 million as printed and label the $23 million as implied, not as letters of credit. - Adjusted measure comparability. Evidence: "Effective January 1, 2026, we are excluding from Adjusted segment EBIT, pension expense related to U.S. and Canada pension plans that we have taken steps to terminate. Prior periods were not recast." (Q3 10-Q page:9). Mechanism: the 2026 adjusted EBIT excludes pension expense of plans to be terminated, which the reconciliation shows as 23,125 for nine months 2026 and nothing for 2025. Consequence: growth in adjusted EBIT and EBITDA between 2025 and 2026 mixes a definition change with performance; CP-1 must disclose the basis and not present it as like for like. - Annual report version. Evidence: later filings cite a Form 10-K/A while the pack holds a Form 10-K. Mechanism: an amendment may restate, add Part III or leave the statements unchanged; the sources do not say which. Consequence: FY2025 figures are taken from the pack 10-K and cross-checked to the December 31, 2025 comparative columns of the 2026 filings (the tie-outs below agree); if the amendment changed them, that is not visible. - Perimeter and the Bank. Evidence: consolidated statements include "Customer deposits at Pitney Bowes Bank" of 576,949 current and 71,000 noncurrent (Q3 10-Q page:3). Mechanism: the Bank is a wholly owned subsidiary (10-K page:6) whose deposits are outside the debt table, and the sources do not give stand-alone issuer, guarantor or Bank financials. Consequence: leverage must state that deposits are excluded from the debt table, and cannot be computed for the restricted group or the borrowers alone.

facts.label: Interpretation: evidence, mechanism, implication
facts.text: - Leverage is lower and moving down through debt paydown. Evidence: debt principal fell from 2,026.2 to 1,918.4 while calculated LTM Adjusted EBITDA moved from 572.9 to 591.5. Mechanism: the 2026 refinancing replaced the 346.7 notes due March 2027 with an extra 150.0 of 7.25% notes due March 2029 and 150.0 of term loan, and a Q3 tender retired 46.5 of 2037 and 2043 notes at a discount (Calculations). Implication: gross leverage of 3.24x is below the 3.54x at FY2025, but the earnings contribution is smaller than it looks, as the next point shows. - Adjusted EBITDA growth is pension-basis driven. Evidence: nine-month Adjusted EBITDA rose from 413.8 to 432.4, an increase of 18.6, and 2026 adds back 23.1 of terminated-plan pension expense that 2025 does not ("Prior periods were not recast", Q3 10-Q page:9). Mechanism: the add-back is larger than the increase; excluding it gives 409.3 against 413.8, and lower depreciation and amortization of 72.1 against 84.5 lifts Adjusted EBIT more than Adjusted EBITDA. Implication: on the 2025 definition LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 568.3 and leverage is 3.38x gross and 2.90x net. This is a sensitivity that assumes the 2025 base carried its pension cost, as the filings imply. - Segment mix is moving. Evidence: nine-month adjusted segment EBIT was 351.2 in SendTech Solutions against 299.3 and 91.0 in Presort Services against 123.3 (Q3 10-Q page:10). Mechanism: SendTech cost reductions and mix offset revenue erosion, while Presort carries higher transportation and fuel costs, with a 15 million fuel and freight increase in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:32). Implication: earnings rest increasingly on the SendTech base, whose revenue is in secular decline. - Cash flow is flattered by working capital and the finance book. Evidence: nine-month cash from operations was 348.2 against 161.6, and the finance receivables line contributed 87.5 (Q3 10-Q page:4). Mechanism: net finance receivables fell from 1,101.6 to 995.1 as the leasing portfolio runs off ("a decline in our leasing portfolio", Q3 10-Q page:30), and management cites prepayments from new Presort customers after a competitor exited (Q3 release page:2). Implication: part of the cash generation is liquidation of an asset base, and prepayments may reverse; the guidance of 380 to 420 for the year implies fourth-quarter adjusted free cash flow of 41.2 to 81.2 against a derived 211.9 a year earlier. - Shareholder returns compete with debt reduction. Evidence: nine-month buybacks of 205.7 and dividends of 40.6 total 246.3, against debt reduction of 107.8. Mechanism: the repurchase authorization was raised to 750 million in February 2026 with 165.9 remaining at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q pages 38-39). Implication: further buybacks reduce the cash available to retire the 2029 notes; the stockholders' deficit is (836.7). - Funding of the financing business. Evidence: net finance receivables of 995.1 and Bank customer deposits of 647.9 sit beside debt principal of 1,918.4 (Q3 10-Q page:3). Mechanism: allocated financing interest of 27.1 for nine months moves cost from interest expense, net into cost of financing (Q3 10-Q page:33). Implication: consolidated leverage mixes industrial and financing debt; no separate financing-segment debt is supplied.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The company is a listed operating business with no sponsor, no acquisition and no leveraged buyout in the sources. Its credit story is one of managed decline: a mailing and shipping technology segment (SendTech Solutions) whose services revenue is eroding with the meter population but whose profit has been lifted by cost cuts, a mail-sortation segment (Presort Services) that is the largest USPS workshare partner and is now losing margin to transportation cost and pricing, and a financing business inside SendTech, run partly through a Utah industrial bank, that funds client leases and loans and is shrinking. The transactions that matter are financing and capital-allocation events rather than ownership events: the August 2024 exit from the Global Ecommerce business, the February 2025 credit agreement, the August 2025 convertible notes, the 2026 refinancing that replaced notes due in 2027 with a larger term loan and further 2029 notes, a 2026 revolver increase to 450 million, a September 2026 tender and term-loan repricing, and large share repurchases. The creditor-relevant change over the period is lower debt and lower interest, a smaller and cheaper cost base, and a leadership and board refresh with activist history, alongside a stockholders' deficit and substantial distributions. Governance evidence is documentary and mixed rather than adverse; legal capacity to add debt, make distributions or release collateral cannot be assessed because the debt documents are not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No acquisition, sponsor buyout, dividend recapitalisation or change of control appears in the supplied sources, so transaction type is Insufficient Information as an ownership event; the relevant events are exit, financing, disposal and distribution transactions. The principal exit is the Ecommerce Restructuring. On August 8, 2024 the company sold 81% of the voting interests of the subsidiary that held most of the Global Ecommerce segment to an affiliate of Hilco, "with a subsidiary of Pitney Bowes retaining 19% of the voting interests and 100% of the economic interests" (10-K page:85, status: completed). The ecommerce debtors then filed Chapter 11 and a liquidation plan became effective on December 9, 2024. The company provided a senior secured debtor-in-possession loan, initially funded at 28 million with 20 million repaid, and the remaining balance is fully reserved; it states that it remains exposed to continuing costs and claims (10-K pages 17 and 85). A vendor dispute arising from the ecommerce business led to a suit filed in November 2024 against the company and a Presort subsidiary seeking more than 100 million, still pending in September 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:24). The financing history is as follows. In February 2025 the company entered a senior secured credit agreement providing a revolving credit facility of 265 million, later increased to 400 million, maturing March 2028, a 160 million term loan maturing March 2028 and a 615 million term loan maturing March 2032, with proceeds used to repay the earlier term loans (10-K page:42, status: completed). In August 2025 it issued 230 million of 1.50% convertible senior notes due August 2030, with a net 221 million of proceeds, a capped call costing 24.7 million and 61.9 million of the proceeds used to repurchase 5.5 million shares (10-K pages 43 and 100). A tender in December 2025 retired 80 million of the 2037 and 2043 notes at a gain of 10 million (10-K page:44). During 2026 the company issued a further 150 million of 7.25% notes due March 2029 on identical terms under a supplemental indenture dated March 2, 2026, increased the revolver from 400 million to 450 million, borrowed an additional 150 million of term loan and extended its maturity, used those proceeds to repay the 6.875% notes due March 2027, and amended the credit agreement in May (Third Amendment), June (Fourth Amendment) and September (Fifth Amendment dated September 29, 2026) (Q3 10-Q pages 20 and 39; Q2 10-Q pages 20 and 40; status: executed and in effect, terms not supplied). In the third quarter it completed a tender of 46 million of the 2037 and 2043 notes at a discount to par and repriced the March 2032 term loan, reducing the margin by 75 basis points (Q3 10-Q page:20; Q3 release page:1). The effect on leverage of the March 2026 notes and the term loan was neutral to modestly negative at first, because 300 million of new debt replaced 346.7 million of notes, and the net reduction came from cash; the effect on maturities is that the first final maturity moved from March 2027 to March 2029 (financial base). In 2026 the additional term loan repaid the 2027 notes; the sources read do not state the use of the additional 2029 notes' proceeds, and in the same quarter share repurchases of 135.6 were paid (Q1 10-Q page:4), a timing coincidence that is not stated as a use. In 2025 part of the convertible proceeds funded share repurchase. The liquidity effect is that the undrawn revolver capacity stood at 427.0 at 2026-09-30 with nothing drawn, after 176.7 was borrowed and repaid during 2026. After the balance-sheet date, pension lump sums of 66 million were paid from plan assets in October 2026 and an intended buy-out of the remaining U.S. plan is planned before year end (Q3 10-Q page:23, subsequent event), and 649,378 shares were repurchased for 11 million from October 1 to 23, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:39, subsequent event). The credit agreement, its amendments, the indentures and the guarantor list are not supplied, so every financing term above is the company's own description.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: a declining meter population and lower leasing revenue (F11), clients extending leases (F12), a management outlook of continued secular decline (F20) and revenue down 2% for nine months. Mechanic: SendTech revenue is a recurring service, maintenance and lease base that shrinks as installed meters fall, and the financing revenue follows the leasing portfolio down; there is bundled visibility of 624.4 (F10) but contract terms are one to five years (F9). Implication: revenue declines slowly and predictably, so debt service depends on cost reduction and run-off cash rather than growth. Counter-evidence: Q3 2026 Presort volume growth and new client wins (F15) are management claims for one quarter, and none of the logged conflicts changes this reading. - Presort margin and cost exposure. Evidence: Presort adjusted segment EBIT of 91.0 against 123.3 for nine months, gross margin down to 31.6%, transportation and fuel costs up 15 million (F13, F14). Mechanic: a network of 34 operating centers and a fleet of more than 350 vehicles is largely fixed, so volume loss and fuel inflation fall straight through to margin, and management expects the pressure to continue in the fourth quarter. Implication: the second earnings pillar is weakening, concentrating segment earnings in SendTech, whose 351.2 (299.3 a year earlier) is 79% of the 442.3 segment total. - USPS dependence without client concentration. Evidence: no client above 10% of sales (F6) but a significant portion of revenue depends on the USPS (F7) and on carrier contracts. Mechanic: postal rates, workshare discounts and the USPS's financial health act as a common factor across both segments. Implication: concentration is in one counterparty's policy and finances rather than in clients; the sources give no contract terms. - Finance book run-off as a cash source. Evidence: net finance receivables of 995.1 against 1,101.6, with a 87.5 contribution to nine-month operating cash flow (F17; financial base). Mechanic: lease and loan collections fund debt service and distributions while the portfolio shrinks, and the Bank's deposits of 647.9 are a regulated funding line. Implication: cash flow quality is lower than operating cash flow indicates, and a smaller finance book also lowers financing revenue. The sources do not say whether any group cash sits in the Bank. - Distributions versus debt reduction. Evidence: buybacks and dividends of 246.3 against debt principal reduction of 107.8 for nine months, and 429.4 in FY2025 (F33, F34, F35). Mechanic: the repurchase authorization had 165.9 remaining at 2026-09-30 and the first final maturity is 476.0 of notes due March 2029 with a springing provision. Implication: the pace of distributions determines the liquidity available to meet that provision; legal limits on distributions cannot be assessed (F39). - Legacy claims. Evidence: the retained economic interest and reserved loan in the ecommerce debtors (F25, F26) and a claim seeking more than 100 million (F27). Mechanic: no accrual is printed and the outcome depends on litigation; management states that the outcome will not have a material adverse effect. Implication: a contingent claim outside the debt figure; it is a monitoring item rather than a quantified loss.

facts.label: Conflicts logged
facts.text: - Term loan and revolver maturity. The Q2 10-Q says the term loan was extended "to March 2031" and the revolver extended to March 2031 (Q2 10-Q page:20); the Q3 10-Q describes the same Q2 extension as "to May 2031" and the revolver as maturing in May 2031 (Q3 10-Q page:20). It affects the maturity profile by two months for the 294.5 term loan and for the revolver, not the 2029 first maturity. - Repurchase authorization. The 10-K says "the Board of Directors authorized a new $500 million share repurchase program" and then an increase "of $250 million" (10-K page:31); the Q3 10-Q says the Board "authorized an increase in our $250 million share repurchase program to $750 million" (Q3 10-Q page:38). Both give a total of 750 million but describe the starting program as 500 million and as 250 million; it counters any statement of how much authorization was added in February 2026. - Margin on the 2028 term loan. The 10-K prints "Term loan due March 2028 SOFR + 2.10% 154,000" (10-K page:98) and the Q1 10-Q prints "Term loan due March 2028 SOFR + 1.85% 152,000" (Q1 10-Q page:18). It affects the cost of the term loan by 0.25% on 150 to 300 of principal. - Tender gain. The Q3 10-Q text says the tender "recorded a gain of $5 million in other (income) expense" while the table prints a quarterly gain of (3,155) thousand (Q3 10-Q pages 20 and 26). It affects the description of third-quarter debt activity by about 2 million.

rows.label: Pitney Bowes is a listed, non-sponsored mailing and shipping technology and mail-sortation business whose creditor case rests on eroding mail revenue, cost cuts, a shrinking finance book and shareholder returns that compete with debt reduction.
No client exceeded 10% of 2025 sales, but revenue depends on USPS and mail volume; nine-month revenue fell 2% and the meter population is declining.
Presort adjusted segment EBIT fell to 91.0 for nine months from 123.3, with gross margin down to 31.6% from 37.2% and 15 million of higher transportation and fuel costs.
SendTech adjusted segment EBIT rose to 351.2 from 299.3 on cost reductions, while net finance receivables ran off to 995.1.
Debt principal fell 107.8 in nine months while buybacks and dividends totaled 246.3, after 378.4 of buybacks in 2025.
Leadership and board changed in 2025, activism is disclosed, and the Ecommerce Restructuring left claims, including one seeking more than 100 million.
Debt principal reduced from 2,026.2 to 1,918.4 in nine months; 6.875% notes due 2027 repaid; notes tendered at a discount; revolver borrowings repaid
Buybacks of 378.4 and dividends of 51.1 in FY2025 against operating cash flow of 383.3, with 61.9 of convertible proceeds applied to repurchase; 205.7 and 40.6 in nine months 2026
Reorganization of the ecommerce business through a sale to a third party, a debtor-in-possession loan and a retained economic interest, leaving claims against the company
Pension de-risking by buy-in, lump sums and a planned buy-out
Leadership and board turnover in 2025 and disclosed activism
Reporting: effective controls opinion, small out-of-period corrections and an annual-report amendment not in the pack
Legal capacity to add debt, make distributions or release collateral
Credit agreement and all amendments, covenant certificates, liquidity and EBITDA definitions
Indentures, guarantor list and security documents
Stand-alone Bank and financing-business statements, and the location of group cash
Pleadings and accrual for the vendor litigation
Mail-volume, price and client-retention data for Presort and meter population for SendTech
Pension funded status and settlement cost at 2026-09-30

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Pitney Bowes is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative mailing and shipping technology credit with a declining revenue base, adequate liquidity and no final debt maturity before March 2029. The strongest support is deleveraging and coverage: debt principal of USD 1,918.4 million is 3.24x LTM Adjusted EBITDA (2.79x net), cash interest cover is 4.34x, and cash plus revolver capacity is USD 695.5 million. The weakest point is the quality of the trend: the 2026 pension add-back flatters earnings, Presort margin is falling, and USD 246.3 million of nine-month distributions exceeded debt reduction. What decides the outcome is whether cost cuts keep offsetting mail decline, and whether the USD 476.0 million 2029 notes are addressed before the springing maturity test applies.

facts.text: Strengths. Deleveraging and low near-term maturities: debt principal down USD 107.8 million in nine months, no final maturity before March 2029, USD 230.0 million of convertible notes that settle in cash up to principal, and term loans due in 2031 and 2032 [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Coverage and liquidity: cash interest cover of 4.34x, cash of USD 268.5 million plus revolver capacity of USD 427.0 million, and the revolver undrawn after USD 176.7 million of 2026 borrowings was repaid [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Client breadth and recurring revenue: no client above 10% of consolidated sales, and USD 624.4 million of future performance obligations, mostly maintenance bundled with leases [Documentary Fact; Business context F6, F10]. Cost reduction: SendTech adjusted segment EBIT up USD 51.9 million for nine months on lower selling, general and administrative expense, the 2025 Plan completed, and corporate expenses down [Documentary Fact; Business context F13, F19]. Finance book quality: about 76% of gross finance receivables are rated low risk and about 1.0% are more than 90 days past due (Calculations) [Documentary Fact; Business context F17]. Issuer behaviour on debt: notes tendered at a discount, the 2027 notes repaid, revolver borrowings repaid, and no priming, uptiering or non-pro-rata exchange appears in the sources [Analyst Interpretation; Business context governance table].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Secular revenue decline: nine-month revenue fell 2%, services revenue is pressured by a declining meter population, clients are extending leases rather than buying equipment, and management expects continued secular decline [Documentary Fact and Management Language; Business context F11, F12, F20]. Earnings basis: the 2026 pension add-back of USD 23.1 million makes the trend flatter than the like-for-like view [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Presort margin: adjusted segment EBIT down USD 32.3 million, gross margin down to 31.6%, a largely fixed network of 34 operating centers and fuel exposure [Documentary Fact; Business context F3, F14]. Cash-flow quality: USD 87.5 million of nine-month operating cash from finance receivable run-off and possible prepayment reversal, with the fourth-quarter implication of guidance [Documentary Fact; Management Language for the cause; Financial base, Business context F16]. Distributions above debt reduction, a stockholders' deficit of USD 836.7 million and a springing maturity test whose liquidity definition is not supplied [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Covenants not verifiable: three maintenance tests exist, compliance is stated, and the reported ratios are not printed [Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on headroom]. USPS dependence: a significant portion of revenue depends on the USPS and carrier contracts, with no contract terms supplied [Documentary Fact; Business context F7]. Legacy and governance: retained exposure to the deconsolidated ecommerce business, a claim seeking more than USD 100 million without a printed accrual, leadership and board change, disclosed activism and an annual-report amendment not in the pack [Documentary Fact; Business context F23 to F27, F38]. Ownership and legal capacity are Insufficient Information [Business context F39, F40].

facts.label: Evidence trace view
facts.text: The traced evidence is sound for the stated purpose of a fundamental, filings-based credit screen. Every dollar figure in the four handoffs was found on the cited page of the cited filing or release, or reproduces from printed inputs, with the exceptions logged in the issue register: two locators that point to the wrong page, one litigation description that goes slightly beyond the note, one coupon-timing explanation that generalizes from a single instrument, one customer description that goes beyond the release, and one date taken from a different page than the one cited. Calculated figures, including the Adjusted EBITDA built for FY2025, reproduce on the release method, which itself ties to the printed reconciliations for every quarter of 2026 and 2025. The weaknesses lie in what the sources cannot show: the covenant definitions and reported ratios, the credit-agreement meaning of liquidity in the springing-maturity test, the guarantee and security structure, the content of the Form 10-K/A that later filings cite, and the executed amendments. Because those gaps bear on committee conclusions about revolver access and legal capacity, the research is graded Restricted, not Passed, and the synthesis confidence of Medium is appropriate.

facts.label: Traceability conclusion
facts.text: The analysis is traceable enough for a fundamental credit screen but not for covenant, springing-maturity, legal-structure or relative-value decisions. Supported claims dominate: the debt schedule, liquidity, maturity profile, segment results, distributions and claims outside debt all reproduce from filed pages, and leverage, cover and liquidity recompute from printed inputs. Inference is confined to labelled interpretation, such as the reading of mail decline, the supportive reading of debt actions and the pension-basis sensitivity. The most important provenance gap is the missing credit agreement: management states covenant compliance and the filings describe a springing maturity, but neither the reported ratios nor the credit-agreement definition of liquidity can be traced. The remediation is to obtain the credit agreement with all amendments, the latest compliance certificate and the indentures.

facts.label: Confidence score
facts.text: Formula: score equals (0.6 times E plus 0.4 times C) times S less P, clamped to 0 to 100 and capped by findings. E is the mean strongest lineage weight over 20 material claims: 10 Directly Sourced at 1.0, 5 Calculated at 0.9, 2 Assumption-Based at 0.5, 2 Analyst Inference at 0.4 and 1 Insufficient Information at 0.0, giving 81.5. C is 17 required registers present of 17, giving 100. S is 1.0 (source gate pass: all seven sources and the context were supplied and read). P is 15 for one MATERIAL finding plus 18 for six MINOR findings, giving 33. Score equals (0.6 times 81.5 plus 40) times 1.0 less 33, or 55.9, rounded to 56. A MATERIAL finding caps the score at 59 and sets Restricted; 56 is below the cap and falls in the Low band (40 to 59).

Issuer: PITNEY BOWES INC /DE/ (Pitney Bowes Inc., Delaware, NYSE: PBI, issuer id pbi). As-of date: 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Current period: Q3 2026 (three months and nine months ended 2026-09-30); prior period: FY2025.

Question for this module: can the supplied source set support the requested downstream work (the financial data and ratio module CP-1, the business and transaction context module CP-1A, the fundamental credit synthesis CP-2 and the evidence-trace validator CP-5), and what remains blocked or limited? This is a source-readiness assessment only. It gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it does not normalize or reconcile figures. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED.

Perimeter: the reporting entity is Pitney Bowes Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries, consolidated (10-K page:69: "The accompanying Consolidated Financial Statements of Pitney Bowes Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries"). The context names no borrower, parent, guarantor, sponsor or deal terms, lists no ratings, quotes or valuation inputs, and attaches no portfolio workbook, management bridge or legal documents (context: legal_documents "none"). Context values left blank are not treated as zero.

All seven sources were read as retained text: 263 of 263 text pages are available (120 + 37 + 41 + 40 + 7 + 9 + 9). The text-page count is a count of extraction chunks; a `page:N` locator is the chunk shown, not a printed page.
### Run context

### Supplied handoffs
None. CP-0 is the first module in this run; no upstream handoff exists. The pack index file `_retrieval.json` is ignored by CP-OS and is not evidence.
### Source profile and original authority

- The 10-K and the three 10-Qs are filed statements and control their respective facts. The three releases give attributed management claims and non-GAAP figures. A management claim does not override a filing.

- Version relationship, unresolved: the pack holds a Form 10-K. The three 10-Qs and the Q3 release refer to the annual report as a Form 10-K/A: "Form 10-K/A for the year ended December 31, 2025 (2025 Annual Report)" (Q3 10-Q page:5) and "Annual Report on Form 10-K/A for the year ended December 31, 2025" (Q3 release page:4). No 10-K/A is in the pack, so which version controls FY2025 facts is not established from the sources (see Gaps). The 10-K cover also ticks the box for "the correction of an error to previously issued financial statements" (10-K page:2).
- The 10-K and each 10-Q are separate periodic reports, not amendments of one another. The three releases are separate management documents. No duplicate documents were found among the seven sources.

- The pack holds no presentation decks (the pack index lists earnings releases in place of decks), no credit agreement or amendment, no indenture, no guarantor schedule and no legal documents. The financing and legal evidence is the issuer's own description in the filings and the exhibit index.

- Extraction fidelity: all seven are text extractions in page-sized chunks; tables are flattened to a line of values. No chart, image or speaker note was inspected, and a successful extraction is not a fidelity review.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The filings and releases cover statements, debt, liquidity, segments, covenants and legal exposure through Q3 2026. All four downstream modules can run, each with bounded gaps. | Medium | No credit agreement, indenture or guarantor list is supplied, and a Form 10-K/A cited by later filings is absent. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Debt by instrument, cash, revolver capacity and covenant levels are printed at 2026-09-30 and 2025-12-31. | Leverage, liquidity and maturity data can be built from filed figures. | High |
| Covenant compliance is stated but the reported ratios are not printed, and the covenant definitions are not supplied. | Covenant headroom cannot be computed from the pack. | High |

| Q2 and Q3 filings give different maturity months for the term loan and revolver, and the Q3 revolver capacity is net of an amount not itemized. | Maturity wall and liquidity must show both readings and a stated basis. | Medium |
| Adjusted segment EBIT excludes pension expense from 2026 only, and prior periods were not recast. | Year-over-year growth in adjusted earnings is not like for like. | High |
### Readiness view

Source sufficiency is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four selected consumers: the financial data and ratio module (CP-1), the business and transaction context module (CP-1A), the fundamental credit synthesis (CP-2) and the evidence-trace validator (CP-5). No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. No missing source prevents any consumer's own method, and no critical identity boundary is unresolved: the reporting entity is the consolidated registrant, named the same way on the cover of every filing (the 10-K prints file number 1-3579 and the 10-Qs 1-03579, the same registrant). The limitations below are source gaps, not findings about downstream analysis, which has not been done. Each limitation is carried into every consumer.
### Coverage of the requested work
| Evidence need | Located in the pack | Assessment |

| Income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, equity | 10-K pages 64-67 (three years of operations, two balance-sheet dates); Q3 10-Q pages 2-4 (three-month and nine-month columns; balance sheet at 2026-09-30 versus 2025-12-31) and page:24-25 (equity) | Adequate; filed |

| Discrete quarters and year to date | Q3 10-Q prints three-month and nine-month columns for 2026 and 2025; Q1 and Q2 10-Qs print their own quarters; the three releases print the quarter and prior-year quarter; the 10-K prints FY2025 | Adequate for Q1 to Q3 2026 and Q3 2025. No Q4 2025 release is in the pack, and no 10-K quarterly table was found; a Q4 2025 figure is derivable only as FY2025 less nine months 2025 on a consistent basis |

| Segments and KPIs | Q3 10-Q Note 3 pages 9-10 and MD&A pages 29-33; 10-K segment note pages 83-84; Q3 release pages 2 and 7-8 (revenue, adjusted segment EBIT and EBITDA, mail volumes) | Adequate; adjusted measures are management measures defined in the notes |

| Facility-level debt and carrying values | Q3 10-Q Note 10 pages 19-22 (seven instruments, principal, rate or margin, maturity, unamortized costs); fair value of debt page:18; 10-K Note 13 pages 97-101 (annual maturities page:101) | Adequate; every instrument printed with principal and rate. Naming and maturity conflicts are logged in Gaps |

| Liquidity, revolver, letters of credit | Q3 10-Q page:20 (revolver $450 million, remaining capacity $427 million) and page:34 (cash $269 million); 10-K page:45 (letters of credit at year end 2025) | Adequate with the letters-of-credit gap in Gaps |

| Covenants | Q3 10-Q pages 20 and 36 (three maintenance tests with step-downs; compliance statement); 10-K pages 42-43 and 99 | Levels printed; reported ratios and Credit Agreement definitions not supplied |

| Cash-paid interest and tax | 10-K page:96 (FY2025); Q1 10-Q page:24 (Q1 2026); Q2 10-Q page:26 (six months 2026); Q3 10-Q page:26 (nine months 2026) | Adequate; the discrete Q2 and Q3 amounts are cumulative figures less the prior period and are not printed as such |

| Claims outside debt | Operating leases (Q3 10-Q page:3 balance sheet; 10-K future cash requirements page:44); pensions and retiree medical (Q3 10-Q Note 11 pages 22-23; 10-K page:44); customer deposits at Pitney Bowes Bank (Q3 10-Q page:3); litigation (Q3 10-Q page:24); letters of credit (10-K page:45) | Described by the issuer; underlying contracts absent |

| Business and transaction narrative | 10-K Item 1 (page:6) and MD&A; Q3 10-Q Note 1 and MD&A; release pages 1-3; Ecommerce Restructuring and DIP Facility (10-K page:85; Q3 10-Q page:24) | Adequate for an operating-company profile; no sponsor or buyout transaction exists in the sources |
### Source-by-source assessment

- **10-K FY2025.** Entity: Pitney Bowes Inc., Delaware, "Commission file number: 1-3579" (page:1). Audited consolidated statements for 2025, 2024 and 2023 (pages 64-67), an opinion that internal control over financial reporting was effective ("maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025", page:62), debt Note 13 (pages 97-101), segment note (pages 83-84) and the exhibit index (pages 56-60). Part III is incorporated by reference from a proxy statement not supplied ("Portions of the registrant's proxy statement to be filed within 120 days", page:2). It records out-of-period corrections ("During the fourth quarter of 2025, we identified an error and recorded an out of period adjustment of $5 million", page:69) and the deconsolidated Global Ecommerce business (page:85).

- **10-Q Q1 2026.** Same entity; three months ended 2026-03-31. Debt table at page:18, covenant text at page:19, cash interest at page:24, segments from page:27. States that segment results were revised for a cross-border contract effective April 1, 2025 (page:5).

- **10-Q Q2 2026.** Same entity; three and six months ended 2026-06-30. Debt table at page:19 (includes a revolver balance of $96.7 million at 2026-06-30), debt narrative and covenants at pages 20 and 36.

- **10-Q Q3 2026.** Same entity; three and nine months ended 2026-09-30; "135,554,541 shares of common stock" outstanding at October 20, 2026 (page:1). Statements pages 2-4, debt Note 10 pages 19-22, pensions Note 11 pages 22-23, contingencies Note 13 page:24, liquidity page:34, covenants pages 20 and 36, exhibits page:39.

- **Releases.** Each release is a management summary of one quarter with segment tables and a non-GAAP reconciliation (Q3 release pages 8-9: adjusted EBIT, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow). The Q3 release carries guidance and a debt-reduction statement. They are attributed management claims; adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow are management definitions.
### Source-risk mechanisms and downstream consequences

- **Covenant headroom.** Evidence: three maintenance tests are printed, including a total net leverage maximum of "no greater than (a) 4.75 to 1.00 for each of the fiscal quarters in 2026" and compliance ("At September 30, 2026, we were in compliance with these financial covenants.") (Q3 10-Q page:20). Mechanism: each ratio is "as defined in the credit facility agreement", and no reported ratio, EBITDA definition or net debt definition is printed. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 cannot compute headroom and must write Not calculable; any ratio they build from adjusted EBITDA is not the covenant ratio.

- **Maturity labels and dates.** Evidence: the Q2 10-Q says the term loan maturity was extended "to March 2031" (page:20) and the revolver was extended to March 2031 (page:20); the Q3 10-Q describes the same Q2 event as an extension "to May 2031" and the revolver "matures in May 2031" (page:20). Mechanism: the sources do not say that a later amendment changed the date; the Q3 10-Q exhibit list shows a Fifth Amendment dated September 29, 2026 (page:39) and the Q2 10-Q lists a Third and a Fourth Amendment (page:40), none of which is supplied. Consequence: the maturity wall must show the Q3 reading as latest filed, flag the Q2 difference, and not state the reason.

- **Revolver capacity.** Evidence: a $450 million facility and "remaining borrowing capacity of $427 million" (Q3 10-Q page:20). Mechanism: the $23 million difference is not itemized; the 10-K says letters of credit reduce borrowing capacity ("Outstanding letters of credit reduce the amount we can borrow under our revolving credit facility", page:45) and gave about $27 million at 2025-12-31, but no 2026 letters-of-credit amount is printed. Consequence: liquidity must use $427 million as printed and label the $23 million as implied, not as letters of credit.

- **Adjusted measure comparability.** Evidence: "Effective January 1, 2026, we are excluding from Adjusted segment EBIT, pension expense related to U.S. and Canada pension plans that we have taken steps to terminate. Prior periods were not recast." (Q3 10-Q page:9). Mechanism: the 2026 adjusted EBIT excludes pension expense of plans to be terminated, which the reconciliation shows as 23,125 for nine months 2026 and nothing for 2025. Consequence: growth in adjusted EBIT and EBITDA between 2025 and 2026 mixes a definition change with performance; CP-1 must disclose the basis and not present it as like for like.

- **Annual report version.** Evidence: later filings cite a Form 10-K/A while the pack holds a Form 10-K. Mechanism: an amendment may restate, add Part III or leave the statements unchanged; the sources do not say which. Consequence: FY2025 figures are taken from the pack 10-K and cross-checked to the December 31, 2025 comparative columns of the 2026 filings (the tie-outs below agree); if the amendment changed them, that is not visible.

- **Perimeter and the Bank.** Evidence: consolidated statements include "Customer deposits at Pitney Bowes Bank" of 576,949 current and 71,000 noncurrent (Q3 10-Q page:3). Mechanism: the Bank is a wholly owned subsidiary (10-K page:6) whose deposits are outside the debt table, and the sources do not give stand-alone issuer, guarantor or Bank financials. Consequence: leverage must state that deposits are excluded from the debt table, and cannot be computed for the restricted group or the borrowers alone.

No new analytical calculation is made in this module. The checks below only test whether printed figures tie, to find source conflicts; their results are not normalized figures. Amounts are in thousands of USD unless a row says millions.

Issuer: PITNEY BOWES INC /DE/ (Pitney Bowes Inc., Delaware, NYSE: PBI, issuer id pbi). As-of date: 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD. The filings print thousands of US dollars; this handoff converts to US$ millions with one decimal (ratios to two decimals) and keeps the printed thousands in Calculations. Current period: Q3 2026 (three months and nine months ended 2026-09-30); prior period: FY2025.

Scope: the financial base for the credit snapshot. It extracts the reported statement lines, the debt and liquidity position, the maturity profile, the claims outside debt and the covenant evidence, then calculates leverage, interest cover and liquidity on stated bases and judges what the evidence supports. It gives no credit conclusion beyond the financial base and no rating view.

Perimeter: Pitney Bowes Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries, consolidated (10-K page:69). The notes name no borrower other than the Company and no guarantor, and no guarantor or Pitney Bowes Bank stand-alone financial data is supplied, so every figure below is consolidated. The consolidated statements include the Pitney Bowes Bank, whose customer deposits sit outside the debt table.

### Corrections and refinements to the supplied handoff

The source-readiness handoff cannot be edited, so its points are checked here. No statement in it is found wrong. Two are refined. First, it logged the unitemized 23 million difference between the 450 million facility and the 427 million capacity as unexplained; the Q2 10-Q prints capacity of 330 million at 2026-06-30 against 96.7 million drawn (page:20 and page:19), which leaves the same gap of about 23.3 million, so the gap is stable across two quarters, consistent with letters of credit but still not stated as such. Second, it logged the 5 million tender gain in the Q3 10-Q text against the (3,155) table amount as an unexplained difference; the principal roll-forward in Calculations shows cash principal payments of 402,032 against 407,778 of observed principal reductions, an implied 5,746 discount to par, which is consistent with the narrative "gain of $5 million" and with a smaller net table gain after other items. The sources do not state this reconciliation, so it remains an inference.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| On the company basis, total debt principal of 1,918.4 at 2026-09-30 is 3.24x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 591.5, or 2.79x net of cash, down from 3.54x and 3.04x at FY2025. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is calculated for FY2025 and LTM, adds back terminated-plan pension expense in 2026 only, and covenant headroom cannot be calculated without the credit agreement. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt principal fell 107.8 in nine months to 1,918.4, and no instrument has a final maturity before March 2029, when 476.0 of notes fall due. | Near-term refinancing need is low, but springing provisions tie the term loan and revolver to the 2029 notes and the 2030 convertible. | High |
| Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was cash of 268.5 plus 427.0 of printed revolver capacity, or 695.5. | The buffer is modest against springing tests whose liquidity definition is not supplied. | Medium |

| Cash interest cover was 4.34x on LTM Adjusted EBITDA against 4.03x at FY2025. | Coverage is comfortable on this basis, but the covenant coverage ratio uses defined terms that are not supplied. | Medium |

| Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA rose 18.6 to 432.4, yet a 23.1 pension add-back applies to 2026 only; excluding it gives 409.3 against 413.8. | Underlying earnings are flat to slightly lower, so leverage improvement rests on debt paydown rather than earnings growth. | Medium |

| Nine-month operating cash flow was 348.2 against 161.6, including 87.5 from finance receivable run-off, while buybacks and dividends took 246.3. | Cash generation is strong but partly liquidates the finance book, and shareholder returns exceed debt reduction. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is adequate for a leverage, interest-cover, liquidity and maturity review to 2026-09-30, on the stated bases and with named restrictions. No consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is printed for FY2025 or for any period in the 10-Qs; the releases print it for Q1 to Q3 of 2026 and of 2025, so leverage is built on Adjusted EBITDA as the Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 releases print it, with FY2025 calculated from the filed segment reconciliation and tied to the release method. The reading is that debt principal has fallen from 2,026.2 to 1,918.4 since December 2025 while LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 591.5 on the company basis, so gross leverage is 3.24x and net leverage 2.79x. Two bases must be shown together: the company basis, and a sensitivity that removes the 23.1 of terminated-plan pension expense added back in 2026 only, which gives 3.38x gross and 2.90x net. Cash interest cover is 4.34x. Covenant ratios, headroom and the springing liquidity tests are Not calculable because the credit agreement definitions are not in the pack. Liquidity is cash of 268.5 plus the printed revolver capacity of 427.0.

### Interpretation: evidence, mechanism, implication

- **Leverage is lower and moving down through debt paydown.** Evidence: debt principal fell from 2,026.2 to 1,918.4 while calculated LTM Adjusted EBITDA moved from 572.9 to 591.5. Mechanism: the 2026 refinancing replaced the 346.7 notes due March 2027 with an extra 150.0 of 7.25% notes due March 2029 and 150.0 of term loan, and a Q3 tender retired 46.5 of 2037 and 2043 notes at a discount (Calculations). Implication: gross leverage of 3.24x is below the 3.54x at FY2025, but the earnings contribution is smaller than it looks, as the next point shows.

- **Adjusted EBITDA growth is pension-basis driven.** Evidence: nine-month Adjusted EBITDA rose from 413.8 to 432.4, an increase of 18.6, and 2026 adds back 23.1 of terminated-plan pension expense that 2025 does not ("Prior periods were not recast", Q3 10-Q page:9). Mechanism: the add-back is larger than the increase; excluding it gives 409.3 against 413.8, and lower depreciation and amortization of 72.1 against 84.5 lifts Adjusted EBIT more than Adjusted EBITDA. Implication: on the 2025 definition LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 568.3 and leverage is 3.38x gross and 2.90x net. This is a sensitivity that assumes the 2025 base carried its pension cost, as the filings imply.

- **Segment mix is moving.** Evidence: nine-month adjusted segment EBIT was 351.2 in SendTech Solutions against 299.3 and 91.0 in Presort Services against 123.3 (Q3 10-Q page:10). Mechanism: SendTech cost reductions and mix offset revenue erosion, while Presort carries higher transportation and fuel costs, with a 15 million fuel and freight increase in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:32). Implication: earnings rest increasingly on the SendTech base, whose revenue is in secular decline.

- **Cash flow is flattered by working capital and the finance book.** Evidence: nine-month cash from operations was 348.2 against 161.6, and the finance receivables line contributed 87.5 (Q3 10-Q page:4). Mechanism: net finance receivables fell from 1,101.6 to 995.1 as the leasing portfolio runs off ("a decline in our leasing portfolio", Q3 10-Q page:30), and management cites prepayments from new Presort customers after a competitor exited (Q3 release page:2). Implication: part of the cash generation is liquidation of an asset base, and prepayments may reverse; the guidance of 380 to 420 for the year implies fourth-quarter adjusted free cash flow of 41.2 to 81.2 against a derived 211.9 a year earlier.

- **Shareholder returns compete with debt reduction.** Evidence: nine-month buybacks of 205.7 and dividends of 40.6 total 246.3, against debt reduction of 107.8. Mechanism: the repurchase authorization was raised to 750 million in February 2026 with 165.9 remaining at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q pages 38-39). Implication: further buybacks reduce the cash available to retire the 2029 notes; the stockholders' deficit is (836.7).

- **Funding of the financing business.** Evidence: net finance receivables of 995.1 and Bank customer deposits of 647.9 sit beside debt principal of 1,918.4 (Q3 10-Q page:3). Mechanism: allocated financing interest of 27.1 for nine months moves cost from interest expense, net into cost of financing (Q3 10-Q page:33). Implication: consolidated leverage mixes industrial and financing debt; no separate financing-segment debt is supplied.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Pitney Bowes is a listed, non-sponsored mailing and shipping technology and mail-sortation business whose creditor case rests on eroding mail revenue, cost cuts, a shrinking finance book and shareholder returns that compete with debt reduction. | Medium | No credit agreement, indenture, proxy statement or legal document is supplied, so legal capacity, ownership and control rights rest on company summaries. |

### Business and transaction view

The company is a listed operating business with no sponsor, no acquisition and no leveraged buyout in the sources. Its credit story is one of managed decline: a mailing and shipping technology segment (SendTech Solutions) whose services revenue is eroding with the meter population but whose profit has been lifted by cost cuts, a mail-sortation segment (Presort Services) that is the largest USPS workshare partner and is now losing margin to transportation cost and pricing, and a financing business inside SendTech, run partly through a Utah industrial bank, that funds client leases and loans and is shrinking. The transactions that matter are financing and capital-allocation events rather than ownership events: the August 2024 exit from the Global Ecommerce business, the February 2025 credit agreement, the August 2025 convertible notes, the 2026 refinancing that replaced notes due in 2027 with a larger term loan and further 2029 notes, a 2026 revolver increase to 450 million, a September 2026 tender and term-loan repricing, and large share repurchases. The creditor-relevant change over the period is lower debt and lower interest, a smaller and cheaper cost base, and a leadership and board refresh with activist history, alongside a stockholders' deficit and substantial distributions. Governance evidence is documentary and mixed rather than adverse; legal capacity to add debt, make distributions or release collateral cannot be assessed because the debt documents are not supplied.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, sponsor buyout, dividend recapitalisation or change of control appears in the supplied sources, so transaction type is Insufficient Information as an ownership event; the relevant events are exit, financing, disposal and distribution transactions. The principal exit is the Ecommerce Restructuring. On August 8, 2024 the company sold 81% of the voting interests of the subsidiary that held most of the Global Ecommerce segment to an affiliate of Hilco, "with a subsidiary of Pitney Bowes retaining 19% of the voting interests and 100% of the economic interests" (10-K page:85, status: completed). The ecommerce debtors then filed Chapter 11 and a liquidation plan became effective on December 9, 2024. The company provided a senior secured debtor-in-possession loan, initially funded at 28 million with 20 million repaid, and the remaining balance is fully reserved; it states that it remains exposed to continuing costs and claims (10-K pages 17 and 85). A vendor dispute arising from the ecommerce business led to a suit filed in November 2024 against the company and a Presort subsidiary seeking more than 100 million, still pending in September 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:24). The financing history is as follows. In February 2025 the company entered a senior secured credit agreement providing a revolving credit facility of 265 million, later increased to 400 million, maturing March 2028, a 160 million term loan maturing March 2028 and a 615 million term loan maturing March 2032, with proceeds used to repay the earlier term loans (10-K page:42, status: completed). In August 2025 it issued 230 million of 1.50% convertible senior notes due August 2030, with a net 221 million of proceeds, a capped call costing 24.7 million and 61.9 million of the proceeds used to repurchase 5.5 million shares (10-K pages 43 and 100). A tender in December 2025 retired 80 million of the 2037 and 2043 notes at a gain of 10 million (10-K page:44). During 2026 the company issued a further 150 million of 7.25% notes due March 2029 on identical terms under a supplemental indenture dated March 2, 2026, increased the revolver from 400 million to 450 million, borrowed an additional 150 million of term loan and extended its maturity, used those proceeds to repay the 6.875% notes due March 2027, and amended the credit agreement in May (Third Amendment), June (Fourth Amendment) and September (Fifth Amendment dated September 29, 2026) (Q3 10-Q pages 20 and 39; Q2 10-Q pages 20 and 40; status: executed and in effect, terms not supplied). In the third quarter it completed a tender of 46 million of the 2037 and 2043 notes at a discount to par and repriced the March 2032 term loan, reducing the margin by 75 basis points (Q3 10-Q page:20; Q3 release page:1). The effect on leverage of the March 2026 notes and the term loan was neutral to modestly negative at first, because 300 million of new debt replaced 346.7 million of notes, and the net reduction came from cash; the effect on maturities is that the first final maturity moved from March 2027 to March 2029 (financial base). In 2026 the additional term loan repaid the 2027 notes; the sources read do not state the use of the additional 2029 notes' proceeds, and in the same quarter share repurchases of 135.6 were paid (Q1 10-Q page:4), a timing coincidence that is not stated as a use. In 2025 part of the convertible proceeds funded share repurchase. The liquidity effect is that the undrawn revolver capacity stood at 427.0 at 2026-09-30 with nothing drawn, after 176.7 was borrowed and repaid during 2026. After the balance-sheet date, pension lump sums of 66 million were paid from plan assets in October 2026 and an intended buy-out of the remaining U.S. plan is planned before year end (Q3 10-Q page:23, subsequent event), and 649,378 shares were repurchased for 11 million from October 1 to 23, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:39, subsequent event). The credit agreement, its amendments, the indentures and the guarantor list are not supplied, so every financing term above is the company's own description.

### Credit translations

- **Revenue durability.** Evidence: a declining meter population and lower leasing revenue (F11), clients extending leases (F12), a management outlook of continued secular decline (F20) and revenue down 2% for nine months. Mechanic: SendTech revenue is a recurring service, maintenance and lease base that shrinks as installed meters fall, and the financing revenue follows the leasing portfolio down; there is bundled visibility of 624.4 (F10) but contract terms are one to five years (F9). Implication: revenue declines slowly and predictably, so debt service depends on cost reduction and run-off cash rather than growth. Counter-evidence: Q3 2026 Presort volume growth and new client wins (F15) are management claims for one quarter, and none of the logged conflicts changes this reading.

- **Presort margin and cost exposure.** Evidence: Presort adjusted segment EBIT of 91.0 against 123.3 for nine months, gross margin down to 31.6%, transportation and fuel costs up 15 million (F13, F14). Mechanic: a network of 34 operating centers and a fleet of more than 350 vehicles is largely fixed, so volume loss and fuel inflation fall straight through to margin, and management expects the pressure to continue in the fourth quarter. Implication: the second earnings pillar is weakening, concentrating segment earnings in SendTech, whose 351.2 (299.3 a year earlier) is 79% of the 442.3 segment total.

- **USPS dependence without client concentration.** Evidence: no client above 10% of sales (F6) but a significant portion of revenue depends on the USPS (F7) and on carrier contracts. Mechanic: postal rates, workshare discounts and the USPS's financial health act as a common factor across both segments. Implication: concentration is in one counterparty's policy and finances rather than in clients; the sources give no contract terms.

- **Finance book run-off as a cash source.** Evidence: net finance receivables of 995.1 against 1,101.6, with a 87.5 contribution to nine-month operating cash flow (F17; financial base). Mechanic: lease and loan collections fund debt service and distributions while the portfolio shrinks, and the Bank's deposits of 647.9 are a regulated funding line. Implication: cash flow quality is lower than operating cash flow indicates, and a smaller finance book also lowers financing revenue. The sources do not say whether any group cash sits in the Bank.

- **Distributions versus debt reduction.** Evidence: buybacks and dividends of 246.3 against debt principal reduction of 107.8 for nine months, and 429.4 in FY2025 (F33, F34, F35). Mechanic: the repurchase authorization had 165.9 remaining at 2026-09-30 and the first final maturity is 476.0 of notes due March 2029 with a springing provision. Implication: the pace of distributions determines the liquidity available to meet that provision; legal limits on distributions cannot be assessed (F39).

- **Legacy claims.** Evidence: the retained economic interest and reserved loan in the ecommerce debtors (F25, F26) and a claim seeking more than 100 million (F27). Mechanic: no accrual is printed and the outcome depends on litigation; management states that the outcome will not have a material adverse effect. Implication: a contingent claim outside the debt figure; it is a monitoring item rather than a quantified loss.
### Conflicts logged
Four conflicts are logged and none is reconciled. Each counters a credit translation only at the level of precision noted.

- **Term loan and revolver maturity.** The Q2 10-Q says the term loan was extended "to March 2031" and the revolver extended to March 2031 (Q2 10-Q page:20); the Q3 10-Q describes the same Q2 extension as "to May 2031" and the revolver as maturing in May 2031 (Q3 10-Q page:20). It affects the maturity profile by two months for the 294.5 term loan and for the revolver, not the 2029 first maturity.

- **Repurchase authorization.** The 10-K says "the Board of Directors authorized a new $500 million share repurchase program" and then an increase "of $250 million" (10-K page:31); the Q3 10-Q says the Board "authorized an increase in our $250 million share repurchase program to $750 million" (Q3 10-Q page:38). Both give a total of 750 million but describe the starting program as 500 million and as 250 million; it counters any statement of how much authorization was added in February 2026.

- **Margin on the 2028 term loan.** The 10-K prints "Term loan due March 2028 SOFR + 2.10% 154,000" (10-K page:98) and the Q1 10-Q prints "Term loan due March 2028 SOFR + 1.85% 152,000" (Q1 10-Q page:18). It affects the cost of the term loan by 0.25% on 150 to 300 of principal.

- **Tender gain.** The Q3 10-Q text says the tender "recorded a gain of $5 million in other (income) expense" while the table prints a quarterly gain of (3,155) thousand (Q3 10-Q pages 20 and 26). It affects the description of third-quarter debt activity by about 2 million.

SendTech share of total adjusted segment EBIT: 351,243 over 442,288 is 79.4%.
- Presort adjusted segment EBIT change: 91,045 less 123,345 is a decrease of 32,300; SendTech: 351,243 less 299,341 is an increase of 51,902.

- Finance receivables: 1,101,575 less 995,101 is a decrease of 106,474, or 9.7% (Q3 10-Q page:11).

- Shares outstanding: 150,703,556 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:117) and 135,554,541 at October 20, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:1), a decrease of 15,149,015 over different dates; during 2025 shares outstanding fell from 182,405,867 to 150,703,556, a decrease of 31,702,311.

PITNEY BOWES INC /DE/ (Pitney Bowes Inc., issuer id pbi), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. This module synthesises the fundamental credit view from the supplied source-readiness, financial base and business-context handoffs, in USD. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
